claim: In the dry three-dimensional model of Shee et al. -- a bidisperse mixture of soft repulsive active and passive Brownian spheres under steady shear -- at volume fraction 0.66 the glass-to-fluid boundary in the plane of Peclet number and active fraction follows alpha*Pe^2 = constant, fitted as about 22 (a second route through the flow curves gives about 17); the same combination, the active energy, also collapses the steady-shear stress and viscosity across a broad range around the transition, the collapse failing slightly at the lowest shear rate.

validity_conditions: A MODEL RESULT. Dry three-dimensional mixture of soft repulsive spheres (a harmonic repulsion approximated by a Morse form), half small and half large (radius ratio sqrt(2)) in both the active and the passive population; active particles are overdamped active Brownian particles, passive ones have no propulsion; kT = 1e-4, Dr = 3 Dt/a0^2 with a0 the small diameter; steady shear with Lees-Edwards boundaries; Euler-Maruyama at time step 1e-2 in HOOMD-blue (version not stated); total strain 10 with the first 5 discarded; no hydrodynamics, no walls, no friction. Peclet number v0/(a0 Dr), which is peclet_number_steric with the small diameter as the length. Shear rates in model units from 1e-6 to 1e-2. Volume fractions (three dimensions) from 0.60 to 0.72. Active fraction from 0 to 0.5 and Peclet number from 0 to 20, ranges chosen to avoid motility-induced phase separation. The glass is identified by a finite yield stress from Herschel-Bulkley fits. The authors read the failure of the collapse at the lowest shear rate as a breakdown of treating sparse activity as one global effective temperature.
